desired_performances: Given a complex technical issue and a non-specialist audience, structure an explanation and adapt terminology to the audience.

objectives.performance: Identify the key characteristics that distinguish a non-specialist audience from a specialist audience in a given communication scenario.
success_criteria: Learner names at least two distinguishing audience characteristics relevant to the scenario.
Learner correctly categorises the audience as specialist or non-specialist.

assumption_notes: Derived from the desired performance; not sourced from a validated framework.

objectives.performance: Structure a technical explanation for a non-specialist audience using a clear logical sequence.
conditions: given a complex technical issue description
success_criteria: Explanation contains an identifiable opening context, body, and closing summary.
Logical dependencies between ideas are sequenced correctly.
No unexplained jargon is present in the structured output.

assumption_notes: Directly maps to the stated desired performance; structuring and adapting are treated as separable sub-objectives.

objectives.performance: Adapt technical terminology to suit a non-specialist audience by selecting appropriate analogies, plain-language substitutions, or definitions.
conditions: given a set of technical terms extracted from a complex issue description
success_criteria: Each identified technical term is either replaced, defined, or supported by an analogy.
Substitutions preserve the essential meaning of the original term.
Audience-appropriateness of substitutions is justified by the learner.

assumption_notes: Terminology adaptation is treated as a distinct procedural skill separable from structural organisation.

objectives.performance: Evaluate a draft technical explanation for a non-specialist audience and identify at least two specific improvements.
conditions: given a provided draft explanation of a technical issue
success_criteria: Learner identifies at least two distinct weaknesses in audience alignment or structure.
Each identified weakness is linked to a specific criterion (e.g., unexplained jargon, illogical sequence).
Suggested improvements are concrete and actionable.

assumption_notes: Evaluative objective included to support transfer and self-correction; model-proposed as an instructional-design convention.

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can distinguish a non-specialist from a specialist audience in a described scenario.

required_evidence.criterion: Learner identifies and labels audience type correctly.
required_evidence.rationale: Direct mapping to obj-tc-01 success criterion.

task.description: Given a brief scenario description, the learner identifies the audience type and lists two characteristics that justify the classification.

scoring.mastery_rule: model_proposed_candidate: both dimensions at highest level; threshold subject to researcher review

assumption_notes: Formative check; no question bank generated; task description is a structural placeholder only.

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can substitute or define technical terms appropriately for a non-specialist audience.

required_evidence.criterion: Each technical term is addressed with a plain-language substitute, definition, or analogy.
required_evidence.rationale: Direct mapping to obj-tc-03 success criteria.

required_evidence.criterion: Learner provides a brief justification linking the substitution to audience needs.
required_evidence.rationale: Supports metacognitive awareness of audience adaptation.

task.description: Given a list of technical terms drawn from a provided issue description, the learner produces a plain-language version of each and briefly justifies the choice.
conditions: no dictionary use unless permitted by instructor

scoring.mastery_rule: model_proposed_candidate: all terms at 'clearly appropriate' with meaning preserved; threshold subject to researcher review

assumption_notes: Formative only; no production question bank generated.

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can produce a structured, audience-adapted explanation of a complex technical issue for a non-specialist audience and evaluate their own draft.

required_evidence.criterion: Written explanation is logically structured with a clear opening, body, and closing.
All technical terminology is addressed through substitution, definition, or analogy appropriate to the stated audience.
Learner self-evaluation identifies at least two specific improvements with rationale.

task.description: Given a complex technical issue description and a non-specialist audience profile, the learner produces a written explanation and then writes a brief self-evaluation identifying at least two improvements they would make.
conditions: technical issue description provided by instructor

performance_levels: clear three-part structure with logical flow
two or more specific, criterion-linked improvements identified
one improvement identified or improvements vague

scoring.mastery_rule: model_proposed_candidate: all three dimensions at highest performance level; threshold subject to researcher review

assumption_notes: Summative task is a structural design placeholder; no production prompt, rubric values, or scoring norms are finalised here.

prerequisites.capability: Basic written and verbal communication in English at a general professional level.
prerequisites.rationale: The desired performance implies the learner can already produce coherent sentences; this is a candidate entry-level gate.

prerequisites.capability: Ability to organise a set of ideas into a logical sequence (e.g., outline or numbered list).
prerequisites.rationale: Structuring a technical explanation presupposes the learner can form a basic logical sequence; flagged as candidate pending confirmation.

modules.title: Structuring and Adapting a Technical Explanation

sequencing_rationale: Module 1 establishes audience analysis as a conceptual foundation before procedural application in Module 2.
Module 2 separates structural organisation (lesson-tc-02) from terminology adaptation (lesson-tc-03) to allow focused practice on each procedural skill before combining them.
Module 3 introduces evaluative and metacognitive skills last, as they depend on having constructed an explanation in Module 2.
Sequencing follows a understand-apply-evaluate progression aligned to Bloom's revised taxonomy levels.

assumption_notes: Module time allocations are estimates; 60-minute total is taken from brief constraints.
Three-module structure is a model-proposed design candidate.

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner will be able to identify and describe the characteristics of a non-specialist audience in a given scenario.
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner reads or listens to a conceptual overview of audience types, then classifies a provided scenario and records two audience characteristics with justification.

assumption_notes: Explanation pattern chosen because the objective is at the 'understand' level; no production content generated.

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner will be able to organise a technical explanation into a logical three-part structure appropriate for a non-specialist audience.
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner examines a provided worked example of a structured explanation, then produces a structural outline for a new technical issue using the same pattern.

assumption_notes: Worked example chosen to make the procedural structure visible before independent practice; no example content generated.

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner will be able to adapt technical terminology for a non-specialist audience using plain-language substitution, definition, or analogy.
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner is guided through a structured process for each technical term: identify the term, select an adaptation strategy, produce the adaptation, and justify the choice relative to the audience profile.

assumption_notes: Guided practice chosen because terminology adaptation is a procedural skill that benefits from scaffolded step-by-step support before independent application.

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner will be able to evaluate a draft technical explanation against audience-alignment and structural criteria and identify specific improvements.
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner applies a provided evaluation framework to a draft explanation (either their own from lesson-tc-02/03 or a provided draft), produces a written self-evaluation naming at least two improvements with criterion-linked rationale.

assumption_notes: Reflection pattern chosen to target the metacognitive and evaluative objective; no evaluation framework content is generated here.

special_review_question: Ignoring machine traceability or schema issues, is this instructional design pedagogically reasonable?
